title: Variance with ABS and tolerance flags
summary: Compare actual sales with plan, measure the size of the gap with ABS and flag only the gaps above a tolerance.

blocks.text: Every Monday the regional manager reviews five stores against their weekly plan. Stores that are far above or far below plan need a phone call. Stores close to plan do not.
Your job is to calculate the variance for each store and flag it when the size of the gap is more than a tolerance. The tolerance sits in an input cell so the manager can tighten or loosen it.

items: Objective: use ABS and IF to flag gaps in either direction.
You pass the mission at 80% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Variance is actual minus plan. A positive result means ahead of plan and a negative result means behind plan.
ABS returns the absolute value: the number without its sign. ABS(-55) is 55 and ABS(55) is 55.
Why use ABS? A store that is 55K behind plan and a store that is 55K ahead both have a gap of 55K. ABS lets one test catch both.
If the size of the gap is more than the tolerance in B8, show Check. Otherwise show OK.
Tip: "more than" is >, so a gap exactly equal to the tolerance is not flagged. Say clearly in the business rule whether the limit itself is allowed.
Four questions on variance and ABS. Type numbers without commas, for example 150 or -45.

items: Variance = actual minus plan; the sign tells the direction.
ABS gives the size of the gap and ignores the sign.
Compare ABS(variance) with a tolerance held in an input cell.
> means strictly more than, so a gap equal to the tolerance is not flagged.
